St. Peter’s Basilica

The must-sees

12 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Church

    Archbasilica of St. John Lateran

    Constantine gave the land for the first basilica in the 4th century, and it is the pope’s own cathedral as bishop of Rome. The popes lived in the Lateran palace beside it for about a thousand years.

    Look for

    Across the square, pilgrims climb the Holy Stairs on their knees; the steps are said to come from Pilate’s palace.

  2. 02
    Fortress · 139 CE

    Castel Sant’Angelo

    Built around 139 CE as the emperor’s tomb, it became a fortress in the Middle Ages. A walled passage, the Passetto, still links it to the Vatican.

  3. 03
    Building · 80 CE

    Colosseum

    Vespasian began it around 72 CE on the site of Nero’s lake. It held about 50,000 people for gladiatorial games and public spectacles.

    Look for

    Read the outer wall from the ground up: plain Tuscan columns, then Ionic, then Corinthian at the top.

  4. 04
    Museum

    Galleria Borghese

    Scipione Borghese collected in the early 1600s. Apollo and Daphne and the Rape of Proserpina are still in the rooms they were made for.

    Look for

    In Apollo and Daphne, watch her fingers turning into laurel leaves and her toes into roots.

  5. 05
    Building

    Palatine Hill

    Legend places Romulus’s founding of Rome here, and later emperors built their palaces on top. The word palace comes from its name.

    Look for

    From the southern edge, look down on the long grassy oval of the Circus Maximus, Rome’s chariot track.

  6. 06
    Building · 126 CE

    Pantheon

    The inscription names Agrippa, but the standing building is Hadrian’s, around 126 CE. It became a church in 609, which is why it survived.

    Look for

    Look up at the oculus, open to the sky, then down: small holes in the floor drain the rain that falls through it.

  7. 07
    Square

    Piazza Navona

    Domitian’s stadium set the oval. Bernini’s Fountain of the Four Rivers, and Borromini’s church facade beside it, turned it into a baroque theater.

    Look for

    The obelisk on Bernini’s fountain is Roman, not Egyptian: its hieroglyphs were carved in Rome for Domitian.

  8. 08
    Building

    Roman Forum

    Temples, basilicas, and the Senate house crowded this valley between the hills. What stands now is the brick and marble skeleton of that public life.

    Look for

    At the eastern end, the Arch of Titus has a relief of soldiers carrying the menorah from the Temple in Jerusalem.

  9. 09
    Church

    Santa Maria Maggiore

    Its nave mosaics date from the 5th century, among the oldest in Rome. Pope Francis was buried here in 2025.

    Look for

    Look up at the gilded coffered ceiling: its gold is said to be some of the first brought back from the Americas.

  10. 10
    Church · 1626

    St. Peter’s Basilica

    Bramante, Michelangelo and Maderno each shaped it over more than a century. It was consecrated in 1626, and the dome is Michelangelo’s design.

    Look for

    Just right of the entrance is Michelangelo’s Pietà, behind glass since a man attacked it with a hammer in 1972.

  11. 11
    Building · 1762

    Trevi Fountain

    Nicola Salvi’s design was finished in 1762. Oceanus stands in a shell chariot; the tradition of a coin over the shoulder is modern.

    Look for

    The two sea horses differ, one calm and one rearing, said to show the two moods of the sea.

  12. 12
    Museum · 1506

    Vatican Museums

    The museums grew from Julius II’s sculpture court. The chapel ceiling is Michelangelo’s, painted between 1508 and 1512.

    Look for

    In the Sistine Chapel, find the Creation of Adam on the ceiling, then the Last Judgment on the altar wall, painted over twenty years later.
